title: Closing an expected failure: strict xfail or skip
intro: E1 is decided and built, and the rebuild test now passes with no marker. Still open is E2 from `rebuild-run-decisions`, asked here as two questions: what to record for the rebuild test (Q1), and the rule for any later gap (Q2). Both have the same two options.

decisions.title: What the record says happened to the rebuild test
decisions.ref: E2 on `docs/reviews/rebuild-run-decisions.json`; commit 663ed74; module 6A acceptance criteria
decisions.context: The E2 page asked how to close the rebuild test's expected failure once E1 landed. E1 landed in 663ed74, and that commit removed the strict marker in the same change; no `xfail` is left under `factory/`. Before that the test was `xfail(strict=True)`. E2 has no ADR, so `records.py` fails on it. The ADR cannot be added until you say which mechanism to record.

options.name: Record strict xfail: the marker was kept until the fix and removed in the same change
pros: It matches the history: the test was `xfail(strict=True)` until 663ed74 removed it with the E1 code
The record then describes what the repo did, so nobody has to reconcile an ADR with the git log
cons: The marker is already gone, so the record is of a finished case and changes no behavior
The record does not say why you preferred strict xfail over skip, unless you add a note

options.name: Record skip: the test should have been skipped with a reason until the fix
pros: Nothing failed or showed as failing while the gap was open
cons: It does not match the history: the test was a strict xfail, not a skip, so the ADR would disagree with 663ed74 and the earlier tasks.md log
The case is closed, so choosing it changes only the wording of the record

decisions.why: Strict xfail is what was done, and the E2 page already recommended it; the ADR then agrees with the git history.

decisions.title: The rule for the next known gap
decisions.ref: AGENTS.md Working rules (acceptance criteria); module acceptance tests
decisions.context: Waves 1 to 3 are not all built, so more criteria may fail for a known spec gap. Checked with pytest 9.2.0: a strict xfail that passes fails the suite with `XPASS(strict)`, a strict xfail that still fails shows as `XFAIL`, and a skipped test is not run and shows as `SKIPPED`. The repo uses `skip` or `skipif` today only for missing tools (Chrome, `srt`, `npm`, `uv`, a live-run switch), in six test files under `factory/engine/tests`.

options.name: Mark the failing criterion `xfail(strict=True)` with the gap named in the reason, and remove the marker in the change that closes it
pros: The test still runs, so a fix that makes it pass is noticed at once: the suite fails with `XPASS(strict)` until the marker is removed (checked with pytest)
The gap shows as `XFAIL` in every run until it is closed
A skip in this repo then keeps its one meaning: a tool is missing
cons: The author of the fix must remove the marker, or the suite fails
If the test fails for a different reason than the named gap, it still shows as `XFAIL` and the new failure is hidden

options.name: Mark the criterion `skip` with the gap named in the reason, and remove the marker when the gap closes
pros: Nothing fails and nothing shows as failing while the gap is open
No one is forced to touch the marker when a fix happens to land
cons: The test does not run, so a fix that makes it pass goes unnoticed and the skip can stay for ever
The gap shows only as one line in the `SKIPPED` summary, next to the skips for missing tools
Under AGENTS.md a criterion is ticked only with test evidence, and a skipped test gives none

decisions.why: A strict xfail keeps the test running and forces the marker out with the fix; a skip does neither.
